profiles.name: Nadine Conner
profiles.excerpt: Nadine Conner carried a nationally heard radio-singing career into eighteen seasons as a leading lyric soprano at the Metropolitan Opera.
profiles.bio_html:
Nadine Conner was born Evelyn Nadine Henderson in Compton, California in 1907 and began serious vocal study while still young. Radio became her first national profession, with featured singing on programs including California Melodies, Shell Chateau and other major broadcasts before opera became the center of her career.

Conner made her Metropolitan Opera debut as Pamina in The Magic Flute in 1941 and remained with the company for eighteen seasons. Her lyric soprano repertory included Mozart, Verdi, Puccini and Strauss, and she ultimately gave hundreds of performances at the Met while continuing concert and broadcast work.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 17 The Railroad Hour broadcasts featuring Conner. Those appearances belong with singers and vocalists because they document the same musical profession that carried her from national radio to the Metropolitan Opera stage.
